FXUS62 KRAH 071835
AFDRAH

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Raleigh NC
235 PM EDT Mon Sep 7 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

* Slightly less hot Wed-Fri compared to yesterday's forecast. Rising 
  confidence in shower/storm chances Fri afternoon/evening and late 
  Sat. Otherwise, no significant changes from earlier forecast. 
  
&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 235 PM Monday...

1) Seasonable early-week temperatures will trend above normal for 
Wed through Fri. 

2) Dry weather through mid week yields to increasing convection 
chances Fri and Sat, perhaps lasting into Sun. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 235 PM Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1... Seasonable early-week temperatures will trend above 
normal for Wed through Fri. 

As a frontal zone progresses further to our S and SW, surface high 
pressure centered over the Great Lakes this midday will build 
southward into central NC as its center slides eastward. Dry air and 
near-normal thicknesses will result in seasonable temps and low 
humidity through Tue. As deep mid-upper level troughing along the 
Eastern Seaboard shifts eastward, renewed mid level ridging will 
build eastward from the Plains into our area starting mid week. 
Slightly above-normal low level thicknesses Wed will climb further 
and peak Thu/Fri with readings around 20 m above normal, supporting 
highs around 2 categories above normal, mainly around 90 to the low 
90s. Heat index values will top out in the 90s to around 100 both 
days. The cold front approaching Thu night and accompanying clouds 
should curb the heat a bit in the NW CWA Fri and areawide Sat into 
Sun. 


KEY MESSAGE 2... Dry weather through mid week yields to increasing 
convection chances Fri and Sat, perhaps lasting into Sun. 

Surface high pressure centered to our N will continue drifting E and 
SE over the Mid Atlantic region and off the coast through Wed, 
keeping us within deeply dry and stable air, with low PWs and no 
pops. While temps will start to warm back up to above normal Wed, 
the 850 mb ridging stretching from OK/TX east to off the Southeast 
coast will limit significant Gulf/Atlantic moisture influx, keeping 
us largely free of rain chances through Thu, although our southeast 
areas could see a few late-day sea-breeze storms Thu. The mid level 
ridge will then break down by Wed night as broad northern stream 
troughing digs over the Upper Midwest and Great Lakes, with its 
accompanying surface cold front approaching our area from the NW 
late Thu, resulting in increasing moisture flux and a rebound to 
near or above normal PW by Fri. With the increasing mid level flow 
helping to boost deep layer bulk shear and increasing low level 
moisture leading to increased daytime CAPE, the confidence in the 
chance for afternoon and evening showers and storms for Fri and Sat 
is also increasing. With the dip in the westerlies reaching down 
closer to our latitude and resulting in passing of multiple weak 
perturbations over NC, these higher convection chances may linger 
into Sun, particularly over our S and E, if the surface front slows 
or stalls over our region. 

&&

.AVIATION /18Z MONDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
As of 115 PM Monday...

VFR conditions are likely to hold over the next 24 hours across 
central NC, with high confidence. A frontal zone has settled to the 
S and SW of the area, with surface high pressure building in from 
the north, bringing drier air. Areas of mid level clouds around 
INT/GSO and westward will slowly exit this afternoon, while 
elsewhere, sct-bkn flat cumuli based at 4-7kft will dissipate early 
this evening, leaving fair to clear skies overnight through Tue. 
Surface winds from the NE or E sustained at 8-15 kts will gust 
sporadically up to 15-22 kts through 23z, then diminish by mid 
evening to under 8 kts. 

Looking beyond 18z Tue, VFR conditions should prevail across central 
NC through at least Thu, with generally dry weather. A few 
showers/storms are possible in our SE (FAY) late Thu, but overall 
the shower/storm chances (and chances for flight restrictions) 
increase starting Fri and peak Sat, as a cold front approaches from 
the NW. 

&&

.RAH WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Hartfield 
AVIATION...Hartfield

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Wilmington NC
220 PM EDT Mon Sep 7 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
The Small Craft Advisory has been extended through 7 AM Tuesday.
Also, Coastal Flood Advisories were added along all coastal 
zones for this afternoon's high tide cycle.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Drier and cooler conditions over the next few days with heat
and higher rain chances returning late week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Drier and cooler conditions over the next few 
days with heat and higher rain chances returning late week.

KEY MESSAGE 1 DESCRIPTION...Sfc high pressure ridging in from
the north through mid week will allow for continued cooler temps
than we've seen as of late, with PoPs no higher than around 20%
and confined to far SE areas/offshore. Temps warm a bit into 
Thursday as the high pushes offshore with some guidance 
supporting 20-30% PoPs inland, but the next good rain chances 
(50-60% PoPs) don't arrive until Friday into the weekend as 
better shortwave energy aloft moves through the area. By Friday, 
heat indices are likely to return to around 100 degrees once 
again with upr-level ridging just off the SE coast.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z MONDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
VFR and dry through the 18Z TAF period. Main item of note is
gusty ENE winds up to ~20 kt for the remainder of this aftn.
Winds decrease tonight then rise again as normal daytime 
Tuesday, but with little change in direction due to high 
pressure still centered off to the north.

Extended Outlook... Predominantly VFR conditions continue with 
dry high pressure in place, with restrictions possibly returning
in convection Friday into the weekend.

&&

.MARINE...
A SCA remains in effect through tonight with moderate ENE flow
as sfc high pressure positions off to the north. Decided to 
extend the advisory until 7 AM Tuesday as guidance typically 
undercuts seas in this regime and they actually already are 
running slightly higher than guidance. At that time and 
thereafter, the 6 ft seas should be confided to around and 
beyond 20 NM. Sub- SCA conditions then for the remainder of the 
week as the pressure gradient noticeably slackens.

&&

FXUS62 KJAX 071843
AFDJAX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Jacksonville FL
243 PM EDT Mon Sep 7 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

For the latest NE FL and SE GA Daily Key Messages please visit:
https:/www.weather.gov/media/jax/briefings/nws-jax-briefing.pdf

- Locally Heavy Rain This Afternoon. Flooding Rainfall Risk
  Mainly Across Northeast FL and coastal Southeast GA. 
  Scattered to Numerous Showers and Storms this Afternoon & 
  Evening. Main Impacts: Locally Heavy Rainfall, Lightning, Wind
  Gusts around 40 mph

- Moderate Rip Current Risk Rest of Today & Tuesday

- Daily Afternoon & Evening Thunderstorms Tuesday to Sunday

&&

.NEAR TERM /THROUGH TONIGHT/...
Highlights Through Tonight:

- Localized Flash Flood Risk for NE FL, including Suwannee 
Valley and North Central FL

There's no shortage of available moisture (precipitable water
around 2.15-2.3") to fuel heavy showers and thunderstorms 
through this afternoon across NE FL, particularly as outflow and
onshore flow interact with a frontal zone stalled near the I-10
corridor. While diurnal heating has destabilized the SE GA 
zones north of the stalled front, the drier aloft will reduce 
the overall storm coverage and intensity, particularly across 
the inland zones north of US Highway 82. Stronger convection and
numerous showers and embedded thunderstorms are expected on the
south side of the boundary in NE FL.

Though soils are not "saturated", soggy grounds persist in localized 
areas across NE FL due to the accumulated rain over the last 3 days. 
This will heighten concerns of localized flash flooding and 
scattered instances of minor flooding through the afternoon. 
Additionally, gusty winds up to 40 mph are possible with some of the 
stronger updrafts this afternoon. Generally, anticipate the ongoing 
scattered convection to push west of I-95 and then progress 
southwestward with numerous showers and thunderstorms developing 
toward the I-75 corridor and into north-central FL by 4-6 PM. There 
will be a break initially this evening but an inverted coastal 
trough, forming over the adjacent coastal waters, will bring a 
chance for coastal showers and isolated storms overnight.

Showers and cloud cover will keep temperatures on the cooler side 
today with highs broadly reaching the upper 80s with some inland 
locations reaching around 90 today.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TUESDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY NIGHT/...
Main Highlights This Period:

- Localized Flooding Rain Threat

- Daily Thunderstorms Chances

The front remains stalled across central Florida Tuesday and 
Wednesday, slowly dissipating. A stronger onshore breeze develops 
Tuesday through Wednesday, keeping coastal high temperatures a 
little 'cooler' in  the mid to upper 80s, while inland highs reach 
the low 90s. Overall, numerous showers and storms are forecast both 
afternoons/evenings inland, with morning showers and isolated storms 
moving onshore, spreading inland throughout the day. PWATs remain 
around 2.0" so the localized flood threat from heavy rainfall will 
continue during this period, we also may see some isolated strong 
storm development over inland locations.

&&

.LONG TERM /THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Main Highlights This Period: 

- Daily Thunderstorms Chances

Precipitation chances remain pretty high (near 60%) Thursday and 
Friday, decreasing slightly this weekend. South/southwest winds will 
rise temperatures back up to above normal in the lower to mid 90s 
through the weekend, with highest storm chances over north central 
Florida. An isolated flooding rainfall threat returns for Thursday 
and Friday, with the Weather Prediction Center having the entire 
area under a 'Marginal' risk of excessive rainfall both days. 
Another front will approach the area from the north at the end of 
this week, at this time it appears to stall over central Georgia 
through the weekend.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z MONDAY THROUGH 18Z TUESDAY/...

There is a possibility that additional convection may develop across 
Jax Metro terminals again this afternoon though confidence has 
lowered enough to remove TEMPO/PROB30 groups for the afternoon 
period. TSRA development remains likely (70% chance) at KGNV this 
afternoon between 19z-22z with storm motion to the southwest 
thereafter. Tonight, coastal showers may reach KCRG/KSSI/KSGJ while 
terminals inland are less likely to be impacted by the overnight 
showers. Northeasterly flow should keep stratus from developing at 
IFR levels but still a 15-30% chance of MVFR ceilings around day 
break Tuesday. Northeasterly winds prevail through the period around 
10 knots at the coast and 5-10 knots inland. Increasing ENE winds 
are expected on Tuesday with gusts up to 20 knots at the coast.

&&

.MARINE...

A front stalls across north Florida today then shifts south of the 
waters tonight into Tuesday as high pressure strengthens to the 
northeast. A brief period of Small Craft Exercise Caution conditions 
is possible mainly over the Georgia waters overnight tonight and 
into Tuesday as a coastal trough develops offshore, then elevated 
combined seas may bring Small Craft Exercise Caution conditions to 
the outer waters on Wednesday as the coastal trough weakens. High 
pressure builds east of the local waters Thursday then extends 
across the Florida peninsula Friday into the weekend with a return 
of westerly winds and the afternoon east coast sea breeze.

Onshore flow will lead to a moderate risk today. As onshore flow 
strengthens and surf builds with breakers up to 3-4 ft on Tuesday, a 
High Risk of Rip Currents will develop along the southeast GA 
beaches. High Risk may expand to all beaches by Wednesday.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...

A cold front is expected to shift southward into central Florida 
tonight, and stalling there through Thursday. Increased rain and 
storm chances are forecast each day, with onshore winds bringing 
morning coastal showers that will spread inland throughout the day 
and increase in coverage. There remains potential for locally heavy 
downpours through mid-week. Overall, dispersion will be fair to good 
Tuesday and Wednesday. Winds will shift to southerly/southwesterly 
Thursday through the weekend.

Fog Potential: Gusty and erratic winds will occur with thunderstorm 
activity. Patchy inland morning fog possible each day.

&&

.HYDROLOGY...

Coastal water levels begin to increase next week with the approach 
of the New Moon on Sept 11th and breezy onshore easterly winds late 
Tonight through Wednesday, with the peak winds across the local 
waters and coast Tuesday. At this time, extended probabilistic 
guidance keeps water levels below action stage late Tuesday through 
Wednesday both along the local Atlantic coast and within the St. 
Johns River basin.

&&

.PRELIMINARY POINT TEMPS/POPS...
AMG  72  90  73  90 /  20  60  20  60 
SSI  78  87  78  87 /  50  60  50  50 
JAX  74  89  75  89 /  40  60  50  60 
SGJ  76  86  77  88 /  30  40  30  50 
GNV  73  90  73  90 /  20  70  20  70 
OCF  73  90  74  91 /  30  70  30  80 

&&

.JAX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
FL...None.
GA...High Risk for Rip Currents from Tuesday morning through late 
     Tuesday night for GAZ154-166.
MARINE...None.

&&

000
FXUS65 KBOU 071806
AFDBOU

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Denver/Boulder CO
1206 PM MDT Mon Sep 7 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Scattered showers and thunderstorms this afternoon and evening,
  a few could be strong to severe over the plains.

- Slightly cooler Tuesday into Wednesday with precipitation
  chances shifting mainly to areas south of I-70.

- Hotter and drier conditions Thursday and Friday.

- Return to more unsettled pattern and cooler weather favored for
  Sunday into Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION /Through Monday/...
Issued at 1153 AM MDT Mon Sep 7 2026

Cloud cover made for a mild morning today, and has also slowed the
diurnal warming somewhat. ACARS soundings show abundant moisture
still in place (PW ~1" currently), and this should only increase
as the day progresses. Instability, which is a notch lower than
yesterday, will likely be maximized within the zone of southerly
flow south and east of the DCVZ. That said, the axis of better 
shear is not particularly coincident, being shifted farther north
over the I-76 corridor where flow aloft will be stronger given 
the approaching trough and jet. This makes it difficult to 
pinpoint one specific area of greater coverage for afternoon 
showers and thunderstorms. In any case, scattered showers look to
develop mid-afternoon over the urban corridor with potential for isolated
and mostly weak thunderstorms. The environment would support some
strengthening into the eastern plains where a few storms could be
strong to marginally severe later this afternoon and evening. 
Temperatures will trend down for most areas given increased cloud 
cover and upslope flow to the north of the DCVZ, with the warmest 
temperatures focused over our southeast plains.

The upper-level trough will traverse the northern CONUS Tuesday,
pushing a weak cold front through the plains and lowering
temperatures 3-8 degrees for most areas. This will also lead to
more stable conditions and erosion of moisture across the northern
half of the forecast area, reducing precipitation chances
considerably. Areas roughly along and south of I-70, where better
instability, shear and PW will overlap, will remain favored for 
afternoon convection and some locally heavy rain.

Drier westerly flow will settle into the region Wednesday as a
zonal pattern takes hold, potentially making Wednesday the coolest
day of the week with highs in the low/mid 80's (only Sunday could
challenge that). Most will stay dry, though a chance of an
afternoon shower or thunderstorm will linger for Elbert and
Lincoln Counties. Those chances evaporate come Thursday as
moisture aloft decreases further. Temperatures look to rebound 
back to above-normal values. Expect little change in those 
conditions into Friday.

Forecast confidence lowers over the course of the weekend as models
begin to diverge in their treatment of an amplifying trough over
the PacNW. Most hint a subtle shortwave embedded within zonal flow
on Saturday and an associated weak cold front bringing initially
cooler temperatures and a return of precipitation chances. The
more significant cooldown however will likely wait until either
Sunday or Monday, depending on the timing of the stronger front 
as the deeper trough approaches and lifts through the Northern 
Rockies. Flow aloft will shift back to the southwest starting
Sunday with a strengthening jet in the mix as well. As such, we 
should see a better window for a return to unsettled weather and 
potentially some stronger thunderstorms and locally heavy rain,
but of course all of those details remain quite fuzzy.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS through 18Z Tuesday/...
Issued at 1153 AM MDT Mon Sep 7 2026

Light northerly winds are expected to slowly turn northeast then 
east-northeast over the next several hours. Mostly cloudy skies 
this morning have slowed warming so far today.ACARS soundings 
still indicate a well-capped airmass and very little CAPE. 
Satellite imagery shows some clearing will move over soon. Decided
to keep the PROB30 for TS at DEN and APA, due to the 
anticipatedclearing and liftfrom the right entrance region of 
the jet. Best chance for storms is on track to be south and east 
of the Denver area. Wind direction late this afternoon/evening is 
expected to be dictated by outflows. Once convection ends, 
northwest winds are expected tonight due to lower surface pressure
over southeast Colorado and cloud cover which will limit cooling 
and disturb the typical drainage pattern. For Tuesday afternoon, 
will introduce a PROB30 for thunderstorms. 

&&

.BOU WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$
